variants.note: Own distinguished_from (california-mission-colonial): 'New Mexico has no tile, no arcade, no arch and no pitched roof: it has vigas, canales, parapets and posts.'
The only roof this variant builds; stated unconditionally rather than region-gated since the whole variant is the New Mexico condition.
Own distinguished_from (california-mission-colonial): no tile, no pitched roof.
The vigas themselves, projecting through the wall and genuinely carrying the roof -- own hard constraint c05: 'non-structural applied viga ends are the single clearest marker of Pueblo Revival.'
No pitched-roof eave assembly exists on the flat-roof condition; the only projection is the structural viga.
There is no eave in the pitched-roof sense at all; the roof edge is the parapet, and water leaves through canales, not a gutter.

eave_condition.rule: The roof has no eave in the ordinary sense: it terminates at the parapet, and the only projection beyond the wall face is the structural viga ends, 12 to 24 in, which must actually carry the roof.

dormer.rule: No dormer. The roof is flat behind a parapet, with no gable or eave anywhere -- own hard constraint c03.

type.value: corner fogon flue, small and low, rather than a freestanding masonry stack

chimney.rule: The chimney is a small flue rising from the corner fireplace, not a freestanding stack of the kind a framed tradition builds; it is a minor roof event, never a principal one.

variants.note: Moulded sun-dried brick in a wooden form -- the Spanish contribution to the older Puebloan coursed-earth tradition.
Not this branch's technique; own description is specific to moulded adobe brick, not tapia.
No coursed stone or brick masonry tradition here; contrast the coquina of Florida or the rubble of California.
No coursed stone or brick masonry tradition here.
No timber-frame branch survives in this variant; even the roof framing is post-and-beam vigas laid on a bearing wall, not a stud frame.

thickness_in.note: Own hard constraint c01; narrower than the parent's general 18-60 in borderlands range.

variants.note: The wall's own material, finished in mud plaster -- the cladding and the structure are the same substance.

Own hard constraint c04: cement stucco on historic adobe traps moisture at the interface and destroys the wall from within -- a preservation failure as well as a stylistic one. Only mud plaster or lime wash is permitted.

foundation_expression.rule: A stone footing carries the adobe brick wall above -- the one place in the wall assembly that is not earth -- own defining_characteristics.

reveal_depth_in.note: Matches this variant's own wall thickness, own hard constraint c01.

reveal_masonry.rule_append: The deep reveal is also the daylighting device: light entering through 2 to 3 ft of splayed adobe diffuses into a warm, grainy glow with no glare, off a plastered surface that has no flat plane and no sharp corner anywhere.

glazed_area_pct_wall_max.note: Own hard constraint c01, narrower than the parent style's general 15%.

variants.note: The opening reads as a hole cut in a mass; there is no arch and therefore no alfiz -- see distinguished_from (california-mission-colonial): 'no arch.'
The alfiz encloses an ARCHED opening; this tradition has no arch on a domestic wall (contrast the Moorish-Andalusian ancestor it is otherwise inherited from).

Restated in this region's terms: a separate flat-roofed block set behind the placita wall or standing at the end of the room-file, entered from the service side, never opening onto the court. The inherited reasoning -- the Spanish house hides what the Anglo house presents -- holds here unchanged.

The file of rooms is additive and grows along its own length before it turns a corner, so a block at the far end of the service arm is native to the type's growth logic in a way an applied wing is not. It stays a block: same wall, same flat roof, same parapet, one more cell in the string.

c02 is hard and limits clear span to 16 ft, the practical viga length; any wider room requires an intermediate bearing and is not of the tradition. A single 18-22 ft vehicle opening can only be got with a concealed steel header, which lies about the one structural fact the entire style is built from. Two bays with an adobe pier between them is the answer -- and it is what groupings/garage-and-hyphen.json already prefers on compositional grounds, arrived at here by structure instead.

c03: no pitched roof, no gable, no eave, anywhere. A shallow shed roof over the bays with applied viga ends stuck under it is the commonest failure and is simultaneously the clearest Pueblo Revival tell (c05, non-structural applied vigas).
The placita is the house's principal outdoor room, not a forecourt. Vehicles stop outside the service gate; driving into the court replaces the one space the courtyard-u plan exists to make.

max_clear_span.note: The viga length. It is the reason a two-car garage in this style is two bays with a bearing pier and not one opening -- the span limit is retrieved, the consequence for the garage is authored.

door_count_preferred.note: Preferred by the grouping and required here by c02. OQ 18, 24 Aug 2026: reclassified from `editorial` to `invented`. The two are different claims -- the schema defines editorial as 'our considered convention' and invented as 'no precedent exists' -- and `garage_strategy`'s own ontology note says in its first sentence that no historical precedent exists. A number about the garage door itself cannot be a convention drawn from tradition, because the tradition has no garage. The parameters left editorial on this slot are the ones carried from the dependency tradition rather than invented for the garage: subordination, ridge ratio, pitch match, cladding continuity.

parapet_height.note: The garage block carries the same parapet as everything else, with not fewer than one canale per roof plane.

wall_and_finish.value: load-bearing adobe on a stone footing, mud plaster or lime wash; cement stucco prohibited
wall_and_finish.note: Retrieved rule, authored application. A frame-and-cement-stucco garage beside an adobe house is the point at which the whole wall system stops being true, and c04 already refuses the finish.

subordination_expression.value: no ridge ratio applies -- there is no ridge; subordination is expressed by parapet height and by the block being one cell wide
subordination_expression.note: The grouping's hierarchy rule is stated as a ridge ratio of 0.6-0.8 and cannot be applied to a flat-roofed, parapeted type. Recorded rather than silently dropped, and replaced by the terms this style actually has.

garage_strategy.rule_append: In New Mexico the block that houses the car is built like every other block in the file -- flat behind its own parapet, drained by its own canale, in the same adobe -- and is held to the 16 ft viga span, so a two-car garage is necessarily two bays with a bearing pier between them rather than one wide opening.

edit_provenance.note: The inherited spanish-colonial-american answer -- detached, behind the blind wall, entered from a service gate -- is right for this node and is kept. What is added is authored: the consequences of the viga span and the flat parapeted roof for a building type the tradition never had.

sources: Authored, not retrieved. There is no historical precedent for a garage in this or any traditional style (docs/inheritance.md).

groupings/garage-and-hyphen.json (two narrow doors preferred over one wide one, doors off the principal elevation, hierarchy rule -- the last of which does not apply to a flat-roofed type and is recorded as inapplicable)
new-mexico-adobe constraints c02 (viga span), c03 (flat roof and parapet), c04 (mud plaster and lime wash), c05 (applied vigas)
garage_strategy.note: Extends rather than replaces: the inherited inward-facing, service-gate logic is correct here; the delta is what the viga span and the parapet do to it.

depth_ft.note: Own proportional_system; narrower than the parent style's general 8-14 ft.

zapata_profile.value: carved wood corbel of a specific New Mexican profile, doing real structural work at the post head
zapata_profile.note: Own diagnostic_tells: 'portal posts with carved zapatas of a specific New Mexican profile, doing real structural work' -- the one place, besides the church portada, this tradition permits carving.

porch_support.rule_append: The post head carries a carved wooden corbel (zapata) that does real structural work transferring the beam load to the post; a decorative bracket that carries nothing is the Pueblo Revival tell.

variants.note: The fogón -- a Spanish-Puebloan hybrid, own defining_characteristics -- rather than a wall-centred hearth.
First Period New England, not this tradition.
This tradition builds a single corner fogon, not paired gable-end stacks.
This tradition builds a single corner fogon, not an exterior-end stack.

hearth_position.rule: A corner fireplace (fogón), small, high and shallow, set diagonally across the corner of the room, burning wood upright -- own description and diagnostic_tells.
